Cyber Attack Disrupts Bermuda Construction Materials Industry

A major cyber attack has struck several leading construction materials firms in Bermuda, causing widespread disruption to operations and impacting hundreds of workers across the island. The attack, which began early Tuesday morning, targeted the information technology systems of companies including Bermuda Aggregates Limited and Coral Isle Concrete, rendering key digital platforms inaccessible.

Company officials report that ransomware demands have been issued, with attackers threatening to permanently encrypt vital operational and payroll data unless payments are made. “Our entire ordering and dispatch system is disabled,” said Daphne Saunders, spokesperson for Bermuda Aggregates Limited. “We are currently unable to process new orders or coordinate deliveries to construction sites. This is having a serious knock-on effect on our production teams and delivery schedules.”

Workers at affected sites say uncertainty is growing as the outage continues. “We arrived this morning and were told we couldn’t access our work schedules or the equipment logs,” said Mark Dill, a batching supervisor at Coral Isle Concrete. “Everyone is worried about how long this will go on.”

The Bermuda Construction Materials Association confirmed that at least four firms have reported significant operational disruption, with some halting production entirely until systems are restored. “This is the most severe cyber incident our sector has faced,” said association chair Linda Perinchief. “We are working closely with cybersecurity advisors and the authorities to restore operations and protect our members’ data.”

As investigations continue, the duration and full extent of the disruption remain unclear. Industry leaders are urging patience and caution among staff while warning that supply delays are likely to persist until the situation is resolved.
